description: LUNAR RESCUE is a NASA Space Apps project focused on lunar terrain safety and emergency route planning. We aim to develop a research-based prototype that uses NASA lunar datasets to identify potential terrain hazards and compare alternative emergency routes. We welcome curious minds interested in space exploration, planetary science, data analysis, design, programming, and storytelling. Beginners and experienced participants are welcome to collaborate!
summary:
**LUNAR RESCUE** is a conceptual lunar landing-site research and planning prototype designed to help users compare potential landing locations near the Moon’s South Pole. We developed a simple dashboard concept that brings important environmental information into one accessible interface.

Users can select two candidate landing sites and an observation date to explore the Sun’s position relative to the local horizon, assess potential solar illumination, and visualize Earth’s position to understand possible direct-to-Earth communication windows. The prototype also includes supporting terrain information to help identify potential surface hazards.

LUNAR RESCUE addresses the challenge by making complex lunar lighting and communication information easier to visualize and compare, helping mission planners, researchers, educators, and the public understand important factors when evaluating landing sites and dates.

This project is important because reliable solar energy and communication are essential considerations for lunar missions, especially in the Moon’s challenging south polar environment. Our goal is to make lunar site evaluation more intuitive and accessible, supporting better-informed mission planning.
details:
LUNAR RESCUE — Project Details

What Does the Project Do and How Does It Work?

LUNAR RESCUE is a conceptual lunar landing-site research and planning prototype focused on the Moon’s South Pole. It proposes a unified, user-friendly dashboard that allows users to compare potential landing sites and observation dates.

The proposed system organizes three key types of information: the Sun’s position relative to the local horizon to assess potential solar illumination, Earth’s position relative to the horizon to evaluate possible direct-to-Earth communication visibility, and lunar terrain context to identify potential surface hazards. Users can compare two candidate locations, represented as Candidate Alpha and Candidate Beta, through a simple visual interface.

Benefits and Intended Impact

LUNAR RESCUE aims to make complex lunar environmental information easier to understand and compare. It can help mission planners and researchers consider lighting conditions, potential communication windows, and terrain-related challenges when evaluating landing locations and dates. It also provides an accessible educational tool for students, educators, and space enthusiasts.

Our intended impact is to support better-informed lunar mission planning by bringing important environmental considerations together in one intuitive interface.

Tools and Technologies Used

We used ChatGPT as an AI-assisted tool for research support, project planning, explanations, and written content. Google Slides was used to design the visual interface concept and presentation prototype. The current version is a conceptual, no-code prototype; it does not claim to perform validated real-time scientific calculations or operate connected hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of LUNAR RESCUE is its unified approach to visualizing solar illumination, Earth visibility, and terrain context within a single landing-site comparison workflow. Instead of requiring users to interpret multiple complex resources separately, the proposed interface presents these considerations in an accessible and organized format.

Factors Considered

The project considers the Moon’s extreme lighting conditions, permanently shadowed regions, potential interruptions in Earth visibility, surface topography, terrain hazards, observation dates, and the needs of both technical and non-technical users. It also distinguishes geometric visibility from guaranteed electrical power generation or successful radio communication.

LUNAR RESCUE is a conceptual research and planning prototype intended as a foundation for future development and scientific validation.
